mainTopic: No מלקות for a broken oath (לאו שאין בו מעשה and התראת ספק), and a לאו paired with a fix-it עשה: the mother bird, the אונס, robbery and collateral
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a case: a man swore to eat a loaf today, and the day ended without his eating it. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree he gets no מלקות. רבי יוחנן says the reason is that it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה. ריש לקיש says it is because the warning was a התראת ספק. Each one reads רבי יהודה's teaching about leftover קרבן פסח meat (נותר) to support his view. Each is then defended with a different tradition of רבי יהודה, and the גמרא explains why רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself. Next comes a משנה about taking the mother bird with her young, where a לאו is paired with a fix-it עשה. רבי יוחנן says there is only one other case like it, and רבי אלעזר finds it: an אונס who divorced the woman. The גמרא works out how an אונס could make remarriage impossible, ending with a vow made על דעת רבים. Finally it asks why robbery and collateral are not on the list, answers that payment replaces lashes, and רבי זירא objects with the collateral of a גר who died.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: no action was done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the person who failed to eat the loaf gets no מלקות because his sin is a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a prohibition that involves no action, and for any prohibition that involves no action, one does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating רבי יוחנן's reason why the man who swore to eat the loaf today and did not eat it gets no מלקות. He broke his oath by sitting still, not by doing something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that מלקות are given only for a לאו broken through a physical act. Here the oath was broken simply by letting the day pass without eating. Since no act was done, רבי יוחנן says there are no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition broken without doing any physical action
They give lashes (מלקות)
Because it is

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets no מלקות is a major principle across ש״ס, and this sugya tests where it comes from.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: because it is a prohibition that involves no action,
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יוחנן's statement from just before: the man swore to eat this loaf today, and the day ended without his eating it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's reasoning, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No מלקות for breaking the oath, because it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reason: the warning was uncertain
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש agrees there are no מלקות, but says the reason is that the warning was a התראת ספק, which does not count as a real warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: He is not lashed, because it is an uncertain warning, and any uncertain warning is not considered a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his own reason why the man gets no lashes. The warning given to him could never be a sure one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות require a proper התראה, a warning given before the sin. In this case, whenever you warn him during the day, he still has time to eat the loaf, so you cannot know he will actually sin. ריש לקיש holds that such a doubtful warning is not a real warning, so no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before a sin, needed for punishment by בית דין
An uncertain warning, given when it is not yet clear the person will actually sin
It does not count as a warning

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree on the outcome (no מלקות). They argue only about the reason.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: He is not lashed,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: No מלקות because a התראת ספק is not a valid warning.

steps.title: Both opinions are based on רבי יהודה's teaching about leftover קרבן פסח meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both אמוראים follow רבי יהודה. It quotes his ברייתא: the Torah put a positive command (burn the leftovers) right after the prohibition against leaving meat over, to teach that there are no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both follow רבי יהודה, as it is taught: 'And you shall leave nothing of it until morning, and what is left of it until morning [you shall burn in fire].' The verse placed a positive command after a prohibition to teach that one is not lashed for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a source both אמוראים rely on: רבי יהודה's teaching about נותר of the קרבן פסח. This sets up the next two steps, where each אמורא reads it his own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving over meat is a לאו, and the Torah adds an עשה right after it: burn the leftovers. רבי יהודה says this placement teaches that one gets no מלקות for leaving it over, because the עשה fixes the sin. The case of נותר also involves doing nothing and an uncertain warning, which is why both אמוראים can learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them, both
According to the view of
Meat of a קרבן left over past its allowed time
A positive command placed after a prohibition, to fix it

steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה on נותר (שמות 12:10)

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's inference: an uncertain warning does count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reasons: the only reason there are no lashes for נותר is the added עשה. Without it there would be lashes, even though the warning was uncertain. So a התראת ספק counts as a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן inferred this way: The reason is that the verse came; but if the verse had not come, he would be lashed. Apparently, an uncertain warning is considered a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן draws a lesson from what רבי יהודה did not say. Since only the עשה removes the lashes, the uncertain warning by itself would not have stopped them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נותר, a warning given before morning is uncertain, since the person might still eat the meat in time. If uncertain warnings did not count, רבי יהודה would not need the עשה to explain why there are no lashes. So רבי יוחנן concludes a התראת ספק is valid, which is why he needs a different reason (no action) for the loaf case.

keyTerms.meaning: Infers, reads a lesson out of the exact wording
The reason is

steps.title: ריש לקיש's inference: a prohibition without action does get lashes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש uses the same reasoning but focuses on the other feature of נותר: leaving meat over involves no action. Since there would be lashes without the עשה, a לאו שאין בו מעשה does get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש inferred this way: The reason is that the verse came; but if the verse had not come, he would be lashed. Apparently, for a prohibition with no action, one is lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש reads the same implication from רבי יהודה, but he learns a different lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving meat over is done by doing nothing. If no-action prohibitions never got lashes, רבי יהודה would not need the עשה to remove them. So ריש לקיש concludes that a לאו שאין בו מעשה can get lashes, which is why he needs a different reason (uncertain warning) for the loaf case.

keyTerms.meaning: This way, so

steps.title: Challenge to ריש לקיש: נותר is also an uncertain warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: the נותר case clearly involves a התראת ספק too. So רבי יהודה's implication should prove that an uncertain warning counts, which goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי שמעון בן לקיש too, this is certainly an uncertain warning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's position. נותר has both features, so רבי יהודה's teaching seems to prove רבי יוחנן's point as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נותר is both a no-action sin and a case of uncertain warning. If רבי יהודה would give lashes there without the עשה, he must hold that the uncertain warning is valid. That contradicts ריש לקיש's own reason for the loaf case. The גמרא now needs to explain how ריש לקיש handles this.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
Certainly
This is (introduces an obvious point being pressed)

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish too,
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון בן לקיש is the full name of ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: this is certainly an uncertain warning!
phrases.notes: He means: so רבי יהודה's teaching should prove to ריש לקיש too that an uncertain warning counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ נָמֵי, הָא וַדַּאי הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק הוּא

steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a התראת ספק is not a warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נותר is clearly a התראת ספק, yet רבי יהודה implies there would be lashes without the עשה. So an uncertain warning must count, which contradicts ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש relies on another tradition of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds like a different תנא's report of רבי יהודה. In that report, a son who strikes or curses two possible fathers one after the other is exempt, so a התראת ספק is not a real warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש holds like the other תנא's version of רבי יהודה's view. As it is taught in a ברייתא: if he struck this one and then struck that one, or cursed this one and then cursed that one, or struck both at once, or cursed both at once, he is liable. רבי יהודה says: if it was at the same time, he is liable. If it was one after the other, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against ריש לקיש from Step 6. It quotes a different ברייתא where רבי יהודה clearly holds that an uncertain warning does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the son hits the two possible fathers one after the other, each warning is uncertain, because nobody knows which man is really his father. רבי יהודה exempts him, so he must hold that a התראת ספק is not a warning. When the son hits both at once, one of them is surely his father, so the warning is certain and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The other תנא, meaning a different teacher who reports רבי יהודה's view differently
At the same time, in one act
One after the other
Liable / exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says which case it is talking about. It is a son who may belong to either of two husbands, so nobody knows which man is really his father.

steps.title: The same problem for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: נותר is clearly a לאו שאין בו מעשה. So רבי יהודה's implication that there would be lashes for it seems to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יוחנן too, this is certainly a prohibition that involves no action!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the same kind of challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. But leaving meat over (נותר) involves no action, and רבי יהודה implies there would be lashes for it if not for the added עשה. That implication seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: this is certainly a prohibition that involves no action!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נותר is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and רבי יהודה implies there would be lashes for it without the עשה. So a לאו שאין בו מעשה should get lashes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן relies on his own tradition of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds like a teaching passed down in his name. רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי, says there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, except for three cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like what רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב עמרם, in the name of רבי יצחק, in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי: for every prohibition in the Torah, if it involves an action, we give lashes for it. If it involves no action, we do not give lashes for it. The exceptions are one who swears, one who substitutes an animal, and one who curses his fellow using God's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by quoting a different tradition of רבי יהודה. This tradition directly says there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as ריש לקיש relied on another version of רבי יהודה, רבי יוחנן does the same. In this version, the general rule is no lashes without an action. The only exceptions are a false oath, substituting an animal for a קרבן, and cursing someone using God's name.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that is broken by doing an action

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא now has his own tradition of רבי יהודה. ריש לקיש's version says a התראת ספק is not a warning. רבי יוחנן's version says a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets no lashes.

steps.title: רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Both אמוראים have been defended. But now רבי יהודה's statements contradict each other, both on התראת ספק and on a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty from רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answers have left רבי יהודה contradicting himself. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will need to deal with the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נותר ברייתא implies two things: a התראת ספק counts as a warning, and a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets lashes. The two other traditions say the opposite: a son who strikes the possible fathers one after the other is exempt, and a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets no lashes. So רבי יהודה seems to disagree with himself on both points.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction: one statement of a sage against another statement of the same sage

steps.whyThisMatters: Defending each אמורא by using a different tradition came at a cost. The question now moves from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש to how רבי יהודה's own words fit together.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty from רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answers in Steps 7 and 9, which rely on traditions of רבי יהודה that clash with his נותר statement
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה's own statements
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נותר ברייתא implies lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה and for a התראת ספק. The other two traditions of רבי יהודה deny both.

steps.title: Each אמורא explains the contradiction in רבי יהודה's views
steps.stepSummary: For ריש לקיש, two תנאים report רבי יהודה's view differently. For רבי יוחנן, one source is רבי יהודה's own view and the other is the view of his teacher, which he was only quoting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you follow ריש לקיש, there are two תנאים who disagree about what רבי יהודה held. If you follow רבי יוחנן, there is no problem: one statement is רבי יהודה's own view, and the other is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 10 with a separate answer for each אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש relied on a different report of רבי יהודה, so for him the contradiction is simply two תנאים reporting רבי יהודה differently. רבי יוחנן relied on a teaching where רבי יהודה quoted רבי יוסי הגלילי. So the 'contradiction' is really רבי יהודה's own view against the view of his teacher, which he passed on. Both אמוראים now stand without a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים who disagree about what a certain sage held
This one is his own view, that one is his teacher's view

steps.whatToRemember: Both ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן survive. Each one has his own way to explain why רבי יהודה seems to say two different things.

phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish –
there are two tanna'im with different reports of Rabbi Yehuda's view.
If according to Rabbi Yochanan – it is not difficult:
this one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
phrases.notes: 'His teacher' is רבי יוסי הגלילי, whom רבי יהודה quoted back in step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ – תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting sources: two reports of רבי יהודה (for ריש לקיש), or a student's own view against his teacher's (for רבי יוחנן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself on התראת ספק and on לאו שאין בו מעשה
steps.terutzMaskana: The two statements come from different reporters, or from רבי יהודה against his teacher, so there is no real contradiction

steps.title: The משנה about taking the mother bird with her young
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says someone who takes the mother bird with her young gets lashes and does not send her away. The חכמים say he sends her away and gets no lashes. Their rule: a prohibition that comes with a 'get up and do' מצוה does not bring lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: someone took the mother bird together with her young. רבי יהודה says he gets lashes and does not send her away. The חכמים say he sends her away and does not get lashes. This is the rule: any prohibition that has a 'get up and do' attached to it does not bring lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about the מצוה of sending away the mother bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says not to take the mother with her young, and also says to send the mother away. The חכמים hold that because there is a positive way to fix the sin (sending her away), the prohibition does not bring lashes. רבי יהודה holds he is lashed, and the sending no longer helps.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking the mother bird together with her young
He gets lashes
He sends the mother bird away
'Get up and do': a positive action attached to the prohibition
This is the general rule

steps.confusionAlert: Watch who says what. רבי יהודה says lashes and no sending. The חכמים say sending and no lashes. It is easy to flip them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic idea of a לאו that comes with a fix-it מצוה‎ (לאו הניתק לעשה). The rest of this discussion is built on it.

phrases.english: We learned in a mishna there:
One who takes the mother bird together with the young,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:6–7

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לוֹקֶה, וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּחַ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: he is lashed, and he does not send her away.
And the Sages say: he sends her away and is not lashed.
This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ קוּם עֲשֵׂה –
phrases.english: any prohibition that has a 'get up and do' in it –
one is not liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: הַנּוֹטֵל אֵם עַל הַבָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion is resolved
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a prohibition that comes with a positive fix-it action does not bring lashes

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: there is only one other case like this
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says this pattern appears only here and in one more place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: we have only this case and one other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן comments on the משנה. He says there are only two prohibitions like this: a לאו paired with a fix-it עשה, where he can still end up getting lashes if the fix is not done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not say what the second case is. That gap is what leads into the next step, where his student asks him about it.

keyTerms.term: אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא זֹאת וְעוֹד אַחֶרֶת
keyTerms.meaning: We have only this one and one other

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: we have nothing
except this one and one other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא זֹאת וְעוֹד אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the משנה in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only two prohibitions paired with a fix-it עשה can actually lead to lashes: the mother bird and one other

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks which case is the other one
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks where the second case is. רבי יוחנן tells him to go find it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: where is it? He answered: when you find it, you will know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks for the second case. רבי יוחנן does not tell him and sends him to search on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next step, where רבי אלעזר finds the answer in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Where? Which one?
When you find it (go look for yourself)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to him: where is it?
He said to him: when you find it.
phrases.notes: Basically: 'Go search, and you'll find it yourself.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case is the 'other one' רבי יוחנן mentioned
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which is the second prohibition that works like the mother-bird case?

steps.title: The other case: an אונס who divorced
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר finds a ברייתא about an אונס who divorced the woman. A regular ישראל takes her back and is not lashed. A כהן is lashed, because he cannot take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, looked carefully, and found it. As a ברייתא teaches: an אונס who divorced her. If he is a ישראל, he takes her back and is not lashed. If he is a כהן, he is lashed and does not take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר finds the second case: the אונס, who is forbidden to divorce the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids the אונס from ever sending her away, and he can fix it by taking her back. A ישראל can take her back, so he is not lashed. A כהן may not marry a divorced woman, so he cannot fix it, and he is lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced himself on a woman and must marry her
He takes her back (remarries her)
Looked carefully, examined

steps.whatToRemember: The second case is the אונס. When he can fix the sin (take her back), there are no lashes. When he cannot fix it (he is a כהן), there are lashes.

phrases.english: He went out, examined carefully, and found it,
as it is taught in a baraita: a rapist who divorced her,
phrases.notes: He broke the פסוק 'he may not send her away all his days' (דברים 22:29).

phrases.english: if he is a regular Israelite –
he takes her back and is not lashed,
and if he is a kohen –
he is lashed and does not take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק דָּק וְאַשְׁכַּח, דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹנֵס שֶׁגֵּירַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question from step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other case is the אונס who divorced: a ישראל takes her back with no lashes, and a כהן is lashed

steps.title: This works for those who say the test is whether he fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the אונס case fits the view that lashes depend on whether he fulfilled the positive מצוה or not. This hints at a problem for the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who teaches the test as 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It says the case fits one version of the rule, which suggests a coming problem for a different version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a לאו with a fix-it מצוה, one view says the test is whether he did or did not fulfill that מצוה. A כהן אונס never fulfills it, so under this view his lashes make sense. The word 'הניחא' signals that the גמרא is about to ask what the other view would say.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view), usually followed by a question on another view
He fulfilled it or did not fulfill it: the test for lashes according to this view

steps.confusionAlert: 'הניחא' is not a conclusion. It says one view works, and it sets up a question about the other view.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who teaches
'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּתָנֵי קִיְּימוֹ וְלֹא קִיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the אונס case against the different versions of the rule
steps.kashyaTarget: How the אונס case fits the rule about a לאו with a fix-it מצוה, under the different versions of that rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case fits the 'fulfilled or not' version. This implies a difficulty for any other version, which the גמרא will raise next.

steps.title: How can an אונס ever make the מצוה impossible?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that lashes depend on whether he made the מצוה impossible, the גמרא can't find a case where the אונס does that and still gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the one who teaches 'he cancelled it or didn't cancel it': with the bird's nest you can find such a case. But with the אונס, how can you find a case where he cancelled it? If he killed her, he gets the bigger punishment, death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the other view, which says he is lashed only if he made the מצוה impossible. It asks how that could ever happen with the אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שילוח הקן it is easy: he can kill the mother bird, and then he can never send her away. With the אונס, the obvious way to make remarriage impossible is to kill her. But murder brings the death penalty, and a person who earns death does not also get lashes. So the גמרא needs a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He cancelled it or didn't cancel it': the view that he is lashed only if he made the מצוה impossible to do
How can you find such a case?
He receives only the greater punishment (so no lashes on top of death)
Sending away the mother bird from the nest

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on the הלכה of אונס itself. It only asks how one specific view (ביטלו ולא ביטלו) can explain רבי יוחנן's second case.

phrases.english: But according to the one who teaches
"he cancelled it or did not cancel it,"
phrases.notes: This means he gets lashes only if he did something that made the מצוה impossible to keep.

phrases.english: granted, regarding sending away the mother bird from the nest,
you can find such a case,
but with the rapist, "cancelled or did not cancel":
how can you find such a case?
If he killed her,
he receives the greater punishment!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּתָנֵי בִּיטְּלוֹ וְלֹא בִּיטְּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the problem hinted at in step 16 for the ביטלו ולא ביטלו view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ביטלו ולא ביטלו view, as applied to רבי יוחנן's אונס case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only obvious way to make remarriage impossible is murder. That brings death, not lashes, so no case of lashes seems to exist.

steps.title: He accepted betrothal for her from another man
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי מחוזנאה suggests the אונס accepted קידושין on her behalf from another man, which blocks his own remarriage to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי מחוזנאה said: For example, where he accepted betrothal for her from another man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי מחוזנאה offers a case where the אונס makes remarriage impossible without killing her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she becomes betrothed to someone else, she is now a married woman and the אונס can no longer take her back. This would be a 'cancelling' act that brings lashes rather than death.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
For example; introduces a specific case
From another man

phrases.english: Rav Shimi of Mechoza said:
For example, where he accepted on her behalf
betrothal from another man.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּיבֵּל לָהּ קִידּוּשִׁין מֵאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by offering a non-lethal way to cancel the מצוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No case of 'cancelling' exists for an אונס except murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: He cancels it by accepting another man's קידושין on her behalf.

steps.title: The betrothal case fails either way
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the case. If she appointed him as her agent, she is the one who cancels the מצוה. If she didn't, his act does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If she made him her agent, she is the one cancelling it for him. If she did not make him her agent, does he have that power? It is nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The suggestion from step 18 is knocked down with a two-sided argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman can only be betrothed with her consent. If she sent him as her agent, the cancelling comes from her choice, not his act. If she didn't send him, his acceptance has no legal effect, so nothing was cancelled at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Agent, someone who acts on another person's behalf
She appointed him
Is it in his power?
It is nothing (it has no legal effect)

phrases.english: Rav said:
If she made him her agent,
she is the one cancelling it for him,
if she did not make him her agent,
is it in his power?
It is nothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שַׁוֵּויתֵיהּ שָׁלִיחַ – אִיהִי קָא מְבַטְּלָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The specific case of accepting קידושין from another man
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Either she does the cancelling or the act has no effect. Either way, he didn't cancel it.

steps.title: He made a public vow against her
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי מנהרדעא suggests the אונס made a vow in public that forbids him from benefiting from her, so he can't remarry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב שימי מנהרדעא said: For example, where he made a vow against her in public.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first answer failed, a new answer is offered: a public vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he vows that he may not benefit from her, he can no longer marry her. Because the vow was made in public, it supposedly cannot be undone. So he himself has made the מצוה impossible, and he gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a vow regarding her (forbidding benefit from her)
In public
Vow

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Shimi of Nehardea said:
For example, where he made a vow against her in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִדִּירָהּ בָּרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 18 with a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The betrothal case was the way he cancels it, but it failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He cancels it through a public vow that forbids her to him.

steps.title: But some say a public vow can be undone
steps.stepSummary: The public-vow answer only works for the view that a public vow can't be undone. For the view that it can, he never truly cancelled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says a vow made in public cannot be undone. But for the one who says it can be undone, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the public-vow answer from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a public vow can be undone, then he can still undo it and remarry her. So the מצוה was never really made impossible, and the case fails for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Undoing or releasing a vow
This works well (for one view)
What is there to say? (the challenge has no answer yet)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
a vow made in public
cannot be undone,
but for the one who says
it can be undone,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בָּרַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a public vow can be undone, remarriage is still possible, so nothing was truly cancelled.

steps.title: He vowed on the consent of the public
steps.stepSummary: The case is narrowed: he made the vow 'על דעת רבים', a vow tied to the public's consent, which everyone agrees can't be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he made a vow against her on the consent of the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the public-vow answer by making the case more specific.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow made 'on the consent of the public' depends on many people agreeing to release it, so it can never be undone. Now he truly made remarriage impossible, according to every view.

keyTerms.meaning: On the consent of the public: a vow whose release would need the agreement of many people

phrases.english: (Where he vows against her) [For example, where he made a vow against her]
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

phrases.english: on the consent of the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִדִּירָהּ עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by narrowing the case of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any public vow; some hold that such a vow can be undone.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow 'על דעת רבים', which can never be undone.

steps.title: אמימר's ruling backs up the distinction
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that a vow made in public can be undone, but a vow made on the consent of the public cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אמימר said: The הלכה is that a vow made in public can be undone, but one made on the consent of the public cannot be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אמימר's ruling to support the distinction it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר clearly separates two kinds of vows. Even someone who holds that a public vow can be undone agrees that a vow 'על דעת רבים' cannot. That makes the answer in step 22 work for all views.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha is (the final practical ruling)
A vow made in front of many people

steps.whatToRemember: The ביטלו ולא ביטלו view finds its אונס case in a vow 'על דעת רבים' that forbids her to him. It can never be undone, so he truly made remarriage impossible and gets lashes.

phrases.english: As Ameimar said: The halacha is,
a vow made in public
can be undone;
one made on the consent of the public
cannot be undone.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר אַמֵּימָר: הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction used in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The difference between a vow 'ברבים' and a vow 'על דעת רבים'

steps.title: Aren't there more cases, like robbery and collateral?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's claim of only two cases by pointing to robbery and taking collateral. Each has a prohibition paired with a מצוה to return.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are no more? But there are! (Memory aid: robbery, collateral, and פאה.) Robbery: the תורה says 'Do not rob' and 'He shall return the stolen item.' Collateral: the תורה says 'Do not enter his house to take his pledge' and 'You shall surely return the pledge to him when the sun sets.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's statement in step 13 and challenges it with more examples of a לאו paired with a fix-it עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said this pattern appears only with שילוח הקן and אונס. But גזל has a לאו ('do not rob') with an עשה to return the item. משכון has a לאו ('do not enter to take a pledge') with an עשה to return it. So it seems there are more than two cases. פאה, the third case in the memory aid, is discussed on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And there are no more? (a challenge to a 'there are only' claim)
Memory aid listing the coming cases
Robbery
Collateral or pledge taken for a loan
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: And there are no more?
But there are!
(Memory aid: robbery, collateral, and פאה)
Robbery, where the Merciful One says
"You shall not rob,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:13

phrases.english: "And he shall return the stolen item."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:23

phrases.english: Collateral, where the Merciful One says
"You shall not come into his house
to take his pledge,"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:10

phrases.english: "You shall surely return the pledge to him
when the sun sets."
phrases.notes: דברים 24:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לֵיכָּא? וְהָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אונס discussion and goes back to challenge רבי יוחנן's 'only two cases' claim from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the pattern appears in only two places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Robbery and collateral each pair a לאו with an עשה to fix it, so there seem to be more than two such cases.

steps.title: Robbery and collateral fit both views too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge from step 24. In robbery and collateral, you can find lashes under the view of קיימו ולא קיימו and also under the view of ביטלו ולא ביטלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you can find it in these cases both under the view of 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it' and under the view of 'he cancelled it or did not cancel it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the question it started in step 24. It says robbery and collateral work under both opinions, so why did רבי יוחנן say there are only two such cases?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two views about when a person gets lashes for a לאו that comes with a מצוה to fix it. One view is קיימו ולא קיימו: he gets lashes only if he never did the fixing מצוה. The other is ביטלו ולא ביטלו: he gets lashes only once he makes the fixing impossible. Robbery and collateral seem to fit both views: he can simply not return the item, or he can destroy it. So they should be on רבי יוחנן's list.

keyTerms.meaning: The view that lashes depend on whether he actually did the fixing מצוה or not
The view that lashes depend on whether he made the fixing מצוה impossible or not
Robbery. The מצוה to fix it is returning the stolen item
Collateral taken from a borrower. There is a מצוה to give it back when he needs it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the second half of the קשיא that began in step 24, explaining why robbery and collateral seem to break רבי יוחנן's 'only two' rule.

phrases.english: And you find it in 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it,'
phrases.notes: 'It' means lashes. You can find lashes here under this view: he simply never gives the item back.

phrases.english: and in 'he cancelled it or did not cancel it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּקִיְּימוֹ וְלֹא קִיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 24 by spelling out why robbery and collateral fit both views
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that only two cases fit both views
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Robbery and collateral also produce lashes under both views, so the list should be longer than two

steps.title: Those cases involve payment, so no lashes
steps.stepSummary: In robbery and collateral the person must pay for the item. The rule is that a person is not both given lashes and made to pay, so these cases do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since he is obligated to pay, the rule is that one is not both flogged and made to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Robbery and collateral are left off the list because the person pays money instead of getting lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robber or lender who keeps the collateral owes money for the item. There is a general rule: אין לוקה ומשלם, one punishment, not two. Since payment covers it, lashes never happen in these cases. That is why רבי יוחנן did not count them.

keyTerms.meaning: Monetary payment, paying back
A person is not both given lashes and made to pay for the same sin

steps.whyThisMatters: אין לוקה ומשלם is a major rule across מסכת מכות. Whenever money is owed, it usually takes the place of lashes.

phrases.english: There, since he is obligated to pay,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the cases of robbery and collateral.

phrases.english: one is not flogged and also pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 24-25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by applying an outside general rule (אין לוקה ומשלם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Robbery and collateral should be on the list because lashes can be found there under both views
steps.terutzMaskana: Because payment is owed, lashes never apply there, so they are rightly left off the list

steps.title: What about collateral of a convert who died?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: there is a case with no payment, the collateral of a גר who died. There is nobody to pay, so the payment answer should not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: But there is the case of the collateral of a convert, and the convert died!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the answer from step 26. He points to a collateral case where no payment is owed, so that answer does not explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 26 depended on the person having to pay. A גר who dies with no Jewish heirs leaves nobody to collect from the lender. With no payment owed, the rule of אין לוקה ומשלם should not block lashes, so this case should be on רבי יוחנן's list.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it. A strong challenge against a statement just made
A convert to Judaism
Collateral taken from a convert

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to it:
But there is the collateral of a convert,
and the convert died!
phrases.notes: The idea is that he died without heirs, so there is nobody to pay back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that payment is why collateral is left off the list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case of collateral exists with no payment (the גר died), so the payment reason fails and the case should count
